Geographic focus:
Europe — Serbia (Deliblatska Pescara reserve, ~80km from Belgrade); secondary reference to Greece (West Peloponnese)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — past fires (1996, 2007, 2023–2025 worst 3-year period this century)
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — ongoing damage assessment, near-term replanting decisions
T3. Long-term development [YES] — 15–25 year forest restoration horizon; increasing wildfire frequency under climate change

Synopsis:
Serbian foresters are developing a multi-year restoration plan for the fire-damaged Deliblatska Pescara sand dune reserve. The core challenge is deciding whether to replant historically dominant but fire-prone species (black pine, black locust) or transition to more resilient broadleaf alternatives. Experts recommend a 3–5 year observation period before large-scale replanting, with the full restoration expected to take decades. The backdrop is a structurally worsening wildfire environment across Serbia, consistent with broader European climate trends.
